title: Mechanical ventilation liberation outcomes
summary: Candidate coordinates for invasive-ventilation duration, liberation, extubation, or weaning outcomes. Ventilation episodes, readiness landmarks, competing death, reintubation, and discharge must be operationalized from observable timestamps.

design_candidates.population: Patients with a reproducibly identified invasive-mechanical-ventilation episode and adequate episode timing.
design_candidates.time_zero: Intubation, start of invasive ventilation, or a defined readiness-to-wean landmark selected before exposure classification.
design_candidates.observation_window: Pre-landmark respiratory support, physiology, sedation, and severity data with episode gaps explicitly handled.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: Follow to successful liberation, reintubation, death, discharge, or a fixed horizon using explicit competing-event rules.
design_candidates.exposure: Question-specific baseline or time-varying respiratory, sedation, or treatment factor measured before the relevant landmark.
design_candidates.outcome: Successful liberation, extubation failure, ventilation duration, or ventilator-free days using a prespecified operational definition.
design_candidates.estimand: Probability, time, or adjusted contrast for the declared liberation outcome in the target ventilated population.
recommended_methods: Competing-risk or multistate analysis when death precludes liberation
Calibration and discrimination for prediction tasks

stop_conditions: Invasive ventilation episodes cannot be distinguished from non-invasive support
Outcome timing cannot be ordered relative to the landmark
Death or discharge status is unavailable for the selected outcome
requires_confirmation: Confirm the ventilation episode and durable-liberation definitions
Confirm how tracheostomy, death, discharge, and transfer enter the outcome
